new_board_item_for_architect.title: Mouse-idle -> Brain: one-brain ambient trigger; retire the local calm driver
new_board_item_for_architect.principle_from_david: The brain feeds ALL autonomous behaviour: brain > body > brain. Even a mouse-idle trigger must relay UP to the brain and be read back DOWN — no local driver deciding what eLo does. (one brain / no parallel drivers)
new_board_item_for_architect.problem: EloIdleBehaviour.cs is a PARALLEL DRIVER: it detects mouse-idle locally and directly plays the Calm pose (animator.speed=calmLoopSpeed 0.28). The brain never knows the user went idle, and eLo's only idle trick is 'calm' — no variety. Meanwhile there are TWO calm paths writing animator.speed for the same clips (meditation 0.3 via EloOSAvatarReceiver.cs:509 vs mouse-idle 0.28), which can drift/fight.

event_contract.UP (Unity -> brain, unity_events.json \u: {'type':'user_idle','idle_secs':<float>,'_ts':<float>} when the mouse is still past a threshold; {'type':'user_active','_ts':<float>} when it moves again.
event_contract.DECIDE (brain, eLo OS ambient engine \u2: Consume user_idle; pick an idle behaviour from a REPERTOIRE by mood/context — calm, look-around, stretch, glance at an app, wander, a soft utterance — not always calm. On user_active, release.
event_contract.DOWN (brain -> Unity, blender_state.json: Write the chosen action through the SAME action path meditation/sit/move already use; EloOSAvatarReceiver executes it. Must compose with WO-041 (verify-before-speak) + WO-035 (a COMMANDED state owns the body; ambient idle must yield, exactly as EloIdleBehaviour already yields to SitHeld).

new_board_item_for_architect.loop_model_from_david: brain > body > brain. A CLOSED LOOP: the brain decides + drives the body (DOWN), the body only SENSES and ACTS and reports its state back UP, and the brain reads that back and decides again. The body NEVER decides on its own. Mouse-idle is just one PERCEPTION feeding this loop — not a special case. The generalisable rule the Architect should check: every body perception (mouse-idle, occlusion/behind-window, perch/surface, user-active, file-drop) relays UP so the brain closes the loop; no local script may choose a behaviour.

Then audit for OTHER local drivers that skip the loop (EloIdleBehaviour's mouse-idle calm is the known one; check for others that decide behaviour without relaying up). Confirm it composes with WO-041 (verify/ACK) + WO-035 (commanded state owns the body).
